title: Label-position map for the zodiac and star pages, made by a non-annotator, so labels can be joined to blind picture annotations
statement: Blind annotators may not read label words, and ZL label line ids carry no position, so on circular and star pages they can say which ring a label is in (the counts match the figures exactly: f70v2 19+10, f72r3 12+11+7, f72v1 20+10, f72v2 and f72v3 18+12, f68r1 29 stars) but not which figure it sits beside; most annotations on the record therefore leave 'label' null or guess an order, and the picture-text statistics (P-L4-013, branch code-P-L4-013-fleet-opus) would have almost no labelled objects. The step: for each of f70v2, f72r3, f72v1, f72v2, f72v3, f73r, f73v and f68r1, a seat that has NOT annotated that folio opens the scan and the ZL transcription and records, for every label line id (unit L), where the label sits: for rings, ring (outer/middle/inner) and clock angle in degrees from the top, clockwise, measured at the label's first glyph; for f68r1, x and y as fractions of the panel. It also records which canvas and which circle it used (f72v2/f72v3 share a canvas and an identical line structure; record which circle carries which ids, which also settles the panel order the annotators had to assume). Output: one JSON file of {locus: {ring, angle_deg} or {x_frac, y_frac}} per folio, submitted as data. The join to picture objects (nearest object in the same ring by angle) is then mechanical and can be added to vs/dsl.py in the same code PR as P-L4-013. Reading the words is allowed for this step because it records positions only, never meanings; the person doing it must not also annotate the drawings of that folio.
check: one positions file per folio; every label line id of the folio present exactly once; ring counts equal the label-line runs between circular text lines; a spot check of three ids per folio by a second seat
